https://www.myjoyonline.com/how-a-sex-sc.body: The Nvidia boss was one of the few business leaders with direct access to the US president. He had met Trump repeatedly, travelled with him to Britain and, in May, joined him on Air Force One for his trip to China. Jensen Huang wasn't just another tech billionaire seeking the president's ear. He had become an important voice in one of the biggest arguments inside the administration: how much of America's most advanced technology should be allowed to reach China. Nvidia makes the chips that power the AI revolution. Washington has restricted exports of its most advanced processors to China since 2022, believing they could help Beijing develop its military and technological capabilities. But enforcing those restrictions is difficult. Chips can be bought legally by customers in countries such as Singapore and Malaysia and then diverted to China. Chinese companies can also rent access to computing power through data centres outside the country. Jensen Huang has long argued that the restrictions are counterproductive. They shut Nvidia out of a huge market and encourage Chinese companies to develop their own alternatives. Trump appeared sympathetic to this view, allowing Nvidia to resume sales of certain chips to China last year in return for a share of the revenue, although its most advanced Blackwell chips remain off limits. The allegations surrounding Jensen Huang's reported affair with Alice Huang, of no relation but a former executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed, have raised the possibility that a foreign intelligence operation was targeting not just a powerful businessman, but someone with unusually close access to the American president. US intelligence reportedly suspects Alice Huang of having links to Chinese intelligence. Beijing has rejected the allegations. Nvidia's board says it has no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised. But the affair has opened up a much bigger question: what did the administration in Washington know, and what did it do about it? His department was responsible for controlling exports of sensitive American technology. It was also being pressed to act on concerns about Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China. On Thursday, Megaspeed chief executive, Tan Yong Pong, also known as James Tan, said the company "takes its compliance obligations under US export control laws extremely seriously" and is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government". He said the company had co-operated with US Commerce Department inspections. A highly classified memo was shared with Lutnick about the concerns surrounding Alice Huang and Megaspeed. He resisted taking action against the company, a decision that is now under scrutiny. Other senior officials wanted a tougher response. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was among those who reportedly questioned why Megaspeed had not been placed on the Commerce Department's blacklist. There were also questions about why an investigation into the Singapore-based company was stopped after Nvidia intervened. The New York Times reported that Nvidia's general counsel contacted Commerce Department investigators probing suspected chip smuggling by Megaspeed, invoking a senior Trump appointee. The department allegedly then froze its investigation and handed the case to the Justice Department. This apparently highlighted a significant disagreement about the direction of Trump's China policy. Huang wanted access to the Chinese market. Other officials were supposedly worried about the national security consequences. Lutnick was caught in the middle. Members of Congress from both parties want answers. Democrats have launched an investigation into how the Commerce Department vetted Chinese companies approved to buy AI chips. Republicans are also questioning the administration's approach. Republican representative John Moolenaar, who chairs the House Select Committee on China, said it was in the national interest for Nvidia and other American AI firms to succeed, but that companies "should never jeopardise our nation's security" by giving Chinese firms access to their most advanced chips. Senator Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, said Huang's resignation did not absolve him of responsibility, and urged Lutnick to explain why export control loopholes remain open. Meanwhile Jensen Huang's team told Republican lawmakers on Wednesday that he plans to cooperate with their request to testify behind closed doors. The White House has not responded to the BBC's request for comment. It has, however, told the New York Post that Trump has complete confidence in Lutnick, describing him as "the most transformative commerce secretary in modern history". That is a fairly emphatic show of support, particularly amid reports that officials are weighing whether Lutnick should be forced out. There are some obvious questions. If Lutnick had indeed been warned about the risks, why did his department fail to act? And if other senior officials were indeed pressing for action, why did it take so long? The BBC has contacted the Commerce Department for comment. But there is an even bigger question for Trump. The president cultivated a close relationship with Huang. He was directly involved in decisions about chip sales to China. And, according to reporting in the New York Times, he was briefed on the intelligence concerns. This is becoming difficult to dismiss as the misjudgement of one businessman or one government department. Jensen Huang's personal life may have triggered the crisis, but the questions now reach into the White House itself. How much influence did he have? What did the president know? https://www.myjoyonline.com/how-a-sex-sc.body_zh: 英伟达老板黄仁勋是少数能够直接接触美国总统的企业领袖之一。他曾多次与特朗普会面，陪同他前往英国，并于5月搭乘美国空军一号随行访问中国。黄仁勋并非又一个试图向总统进言的科技富豪。他已成为本届政府内部最大争论之一中的重要声音：美国应允许多少最先进技术流入中国？英伟达制造驱动人工智能革命的芯片。自2022年以来，华盛顿一直限制英伟达向中国出口最先进的处理器，认为这些芯片可能帮助北京发展军事和技术能力。但执行这些限制并不容易。客户可以在新加坡、马来西亚等国家合法购买芯片，随后转售至中国。中国企业还可通过租用境外数据中心的算力来获取计算资源。黄仁勋长期认为，这些限制会适得其反。它们让英伟达被排除在一个庞大市场之外，并促使中国企业开发自己的替代产品。特朗普似乎认同这一观点，去年允许英伟达恢复向中国销售部分芯片，以换取部分收入分成，但其最先进的Blackwell芯片仍禁止出口。有关黄仁勋据报与Alice Huang有婚外情的指控掀起了更多疑问。Alice Huang与黄仁勋没有亲属关系，曾任职于总部位于新加坡的公司Megaspeed。这些指控表明，外国情报行动的针对目标可能不仅是一位权势显赫的商人，还是一位与关系异常密切的美国总统接触频繁的人。据报道，美国情报部门怀疑Alice Huang与中国情报机构有关联。北京否认了这些指控。英伟达董事会表示，没有理由相信公司机密或国家安全受到损害。但这段婚外情引出了一个更大的问题：华盛顿政府知道多少，又采取了什么措施？他的部门负责管制美国敏感技术出口。与此同时，该部门还面临压力，需要就Megaspeed引发的担忧采取行动。这家英伟达客户被怀疑协助将先进芯片转运至中国。周四，Megaspeed首席执行官Tan Yong Pong（又名James Tan）表示，公司“极其认真地履行美国出口管制法律规定的合规义务”，并“致力于与美国政府建设性、透明地合作”。他说，公司曾配合美国商务部检查。一份高度机密的备忘录被提交给Lutnick，内容涉及围绕Alice Huang和Megaspeed的担忧。他拒绝对该公司采取行动，而这一决定如今正受到审视。其他高级官员希望采取更强硬的回应。据报道，财政部长Scott Bessent也在质疑者之列，他问Megaspeed为何未被列入商务部黑名单。还有人追问，在英伟达介入后，为何针对这家新加坡公司的调查会被终止。《纽约时报》报道，英伟达总法律顾问联系了调查Megaspeed涉嫌走私芯片的商务部调查人员，并援引了一位由特朗普任命的高级官员。随后，据称该部门暂停调查，并将案件移交司法部。这似乎凸显了特朗普对华政策方向上的重大分歧。黄仁勋希望获得中国市场准入，而其他官员则担心可能产生的国家安全后果。Lutnick夹在中间。两党议员都要求得到答案。民主党人对商务部如何审查获准购买人工智能芯片的中国企业展开调查，共和党人也在质疑本届政府的做法。共和党众议员John Moolenaar担任众议院中国问题特别委员会主席。他说，让英伟达和其他美国人工智能企业取得成功符合国家利益，但企业“绝不应”因向中国企业提供其最先进芯片的使用权而危及国家安全。参议院银行委员会首席民主党参议员Elizabeth Warren表示，黄仁勋辞职并不能免除他的责任，并敦促Lutnick解释出口管制漏洞为何仍未堵住。与此同时，黄仁勋的团队周三告诉共和党议员，他计划配合他们的要求，闭门作证。白宫尚未回应BBC的置评请求。不过，白宫告诉《纽约邮报》，特朗普完全信任Lutnick，称他是“现代历史上最具变革性的商务部长”。这是相当有力的支持，尤其是在有报道称官员正在权衡是否应迫使Lutnick下台之际。这里有一些显而易见的问题。如果Lutnick确实曾获警告风险，他的部门为何没有采取行动？如果其他高级官员确实在敦促采取行动，为何要等那么久？BBC已联系商务部置评。但对特朗普而言，还有一个更大的问题。总统与黄仁勋建立了密切关系，并直接参与了有关向中国销售芯片的决策。据《纽约时报》报道，他曾听取有关情报方面担忧的简报。这越来越难以被解释为单个商人或单个政府部门的误判。黄仁勋的个人生活可能触发了这场危机，但如今相关问题已延伸至白宫本身。他对政府有多大影响力？总统知道什么？最终，谁负责保护美国最敏感的技术？
